Orthonormality is a special case of [[orthogonality]].

== Mathematical definition ==

Let [[vector space]] $V$ be an [[inner product space]].

If for $u,v\in V$

$$
\begin{cases}
\langle u, v \rangle=0 & \text{(orthogonality)} \\
\langle u, u \rangle=1 \land \langle v, v \rangle=1 & \text{(normality)}
\end{cases}
$$

Then $u,v$ are '''orthonormal''' to each other.
<ref>{{#cite:Q1930}}</ref>

== Orthonormal vector list ==

A list of '''nonzero''' vectors $(e_1,\ldots,e_m) \in V$ is '''orthonormal''' if

$$
\langle e_i, e_j \rangle = \delta_{i,j} \Leftarrow i,j \in \{1,m\}
$$

where $\delta_{ij}$ is the [[Kronecker delta function]], i.e., $\delta_{ij} = \text{ if } i=j \text{ otherwise } 0$.

which means:

$$
\langle e_i, e_j \rangle = 0 \Leftarrow 1\le i\neq j \le m & \text{(orthogonality)}\\
\langle e_i, e_i \rangle = 1 \Leftarrow 1\le i \le m & \text{(normality)}
$$
